data.why: The app ships two sanitized Pt/Al-MFI extended-XYZ trajectories (examples/T04_1200K.xyz, examples/T08_1200K.xyz, ~545 KB each) that load automatically in 'Built-in examples' mode on first run, so no files need to be staged for upload; each is too large to duplicate as a <200KB prep/data file anyway.

goals: Load a multi-frame extended-XYZ trajectory and visually inspect the 3D periodic structure (rotate, zoom, pan, toggle unit cell)
Compare two trajectories side by side in synchronized playback to see how atomic configurations diverge over time
Select specific elements or atom indices and switch between ball-and-stick, space-filling, and framework representations to study local coordination
Measure element-pair distances and coordination numbers (e.g., Pt-Pt, Pt-O) across frames using periodic-boundary-aware ASE neighbor lists
Run the Pt/Al-MFI analysis preset to track Pt cluster span and Pt-O coordination as a proxy for sintering/dispersion behavior, with the built-in scientific disclaimer in view
Upload one's own multi-frame XYZ trajectory (optionally with Lattice/pbc/Time metadata) and reproduce the same inspection and pair-analysis workflow on it

review.summary: The tree captures the tool's purpose well: periodic 3D inspection and synced two-trajectory comparison, with tidy, well-evidenced tasks for viewing, picking atoms and cropping to a local environment. The quantify half needs work: it mixes the generic pair analysis with the Pt preset, claims a frame marker that doesn't move and a reset that only half works, cites a stale stalled-server screen as a result, and leaves out upload and custom pair cutoffs.
